Restore a service from a backup

Take a service that has lost its data back to a known-good state: choose a snapshot, restore it into a staging target, check it, then promote it. The procedure ends when the service reports healthy against the restored data.

Draft
Recovery

This template describes an imaginary product and records nothing that was performed. It exists to demonstrate the shape.

At a glance

Phase Where What it achieves
0 Choose a snapshot A snapshot id, and evidence that it completed
1 Restore into staging A staging target holding the restored data
2 Promote the target Live traffic served from the restored data
Phase 0

Choose a snapshot

  1. Go to Console
  2. Backup and Recovery
  3. Snapshots
# Do this You should see
0.1 Open
Snapshots
and filter to the affected service		 A list ordered newest first, each row carrying a size and a completed time
0.2 Choose the newest snapshot whose state reads
Complete
 The row expands to show the byte count and the checksum
0.3 Copy the snapshot id into the run record below An id of the form
snap-0000-0000
0.4 Export the manifest for the record
Optional
 A file download, named for the snapshot id
Phase 1

Restore into staging

  1. Go to Console
  2. Backup and Recovery
  3. Restore
  4. New Restore Job
Note
A restore never writes over the live target. It builds a second one, which is what makes phase 2 a decision rather than a consequence.
# Do this You should see
1.1 Start a restore job against the snapshot id from 0.3 The job appears as
Running
with an estimate
1.2 Wait for it to finish, then open the new target A target named for the job, holding the restored data
1.3 Run the service's own consistency check against it Every check passes, and the row count matches the manifest
Phase 2

Promote the target

  1. Go to Console
  2. Services
  3. Routing and Targets
This step cannot be undone
Promotion retires the previous target. Anything written to it after the snapshot was taken is not carried across, and there is no second promotion back.
# Do this You should see
2.1 Point the service at the restored target The routing entry names the new target
2.2 Choose
Promote
and confirm		 The previous target moves to
Retired
2.3 Watch the service's health for one full check interval The service reads
Healthy
against the restored data

Fill each row in as its step is reached. The From column names the step that produces the value.

Troubleshooting

Phase Symptom Cause
0 No snapshot reads
Complete
 The schedule is paused, so every snapshot listed was cancelled part way
1 The consistency check fails on a restored target The snapshot was taken during a write, and only a quiesced one is safe to restore
2 Health stays amber after promotion The service caches its target for one check interval; longer than that is a real fault
